Against The Judgment And Award Dated: 02.12.2013
Passed In Mvc No.682/2008 On The File Of The Senior
Civil Judge, Member, Addl. Mact, Kundapura, Awarding
A Compensation Of Rs.3,64,500/- With Interest @ 6% P.A
From The Date Of Petition Till The Date Of Deposit
With The Tribunal.

This Mfa Having Been Heard And Reserved For
Judgment On 09.06.2023 And Coming On For
Pronouncement Of Judgment This Day, The Court
Delivered The Following:

Mfa.No.2879/2014
 3
 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' in short), is filed by the NWKRTC ('the Corporation' for short) against the judgment and award dated 02.12.2013 passed in M.V.C.No.682/2008 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Kundapura ('the Tribunal'
in short).
2. Appellant was the respondent No.4 and respondent Nos.1 to 3 were the petitioner Nos.2 to 4 and respondent Nos.4 to 6 were the respondent Nos.1 to 3 before the Tribunal.

The petitioner No.1 was The Divisional Controller vs Madhu on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165861954/
2 dead.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case is that, on 12.04.2008 one Laxman ('the deceased' for short), who is the son of petitioner No.1 and brother of petitioner Nos. 2 to 4, boarded the bus bearing No.KA-31/3172 at Byndoor.
At about 11.00 a.m., the bus reached Nagoor Bus Stop.

The deceased was about to get down from the said bus, at that time, the first respondent being the driver of the bus hurriedly moved it, due to which, the deceased fell down from the bus, sustained injuries and succumbed to death on the way to Manipal hospital.

Petitioner Nos.2 to 4, who are the brothers of deceased, along with their mother petitioner No.1 presented a petition under Section 163-A of the Act on the ground that they spent Rs.10,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.2,000/- towards conveyance charges and Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses.
It is also contended that the deceased was working as an Electrician in Pooja Electricals, Kundapura, earning Rs.40,000/- per annum.
The petitioners lost love and affection and sought for award of Rs.10,37,000/-.
4. The claim was opposed by the respondent remained exparte.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence of the parties and hearing both sides passed the impugned order awarding Rs.3,64,500/-
as compensation with interest @ 6% per annum directing that the fourth respondent/Corporation is liable to pay the compensation and dismissed the claim against respondent Nos.1 to 3.
Aggrieved by fastening of the liability against it, the Corporation has filed this appeal on various grounds.
5. I have heard the arguments of Sri.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for the Corporation and Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for respondent No.3/insurer.

6. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Corporation that Section 103(1-A) of the Karnataka Amendment to Motor Vehicles Act, contemplates that the bus being hired to the State Transport having authority to ply in route under any term and therefore, the Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the Corporation has to pay the compensation and sought for a direction to the 6th respondent/insurer to pay the compensation.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel further contended that the income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.40,000/- per annum and selection of multiplier at '18' is on higher side and sought for reduction of the compensation.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurer has contended that even though the bus was covered with insurance by the third respondent, insured to the second respondent, the bus was hired to the fourth respondent/Corporation, the contract of hiring was not informed to the insurer, there is no incorporation of terms of hiring in the policy and the appeal is filed belatedly by 45 days and the interest component has to be excluded for that and in view of violation of the terms of the policy, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability against the Corporation and the Insurance Company has no liability to indemnify the owner in the facts and circumstances of the case.
8.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

3 9.
Firstly, under Section 163-A of the Act, the income as well as the multiplier is pre
- determined.
The records point out that the deceased was aged 23 years and the first petitioner Fusi was the mother aged 50 years and petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are the minor brothers of the deceased.
They are all the dependants of the deceased.
The Tribunal has taken the multiplier of '18' and having regard to the status of the petitioners, selection of multiplier is proper, as there are four dependants.
Under Section 163-A of the Act, the maximum notional income shall not exceed Rs.40,000/- per annum.
The deceased was an Electrician working in Pooja Electricals at Kundapura.
The Tribunal has rightly taken the income at Rs.40,000/- per annum.

Though the deceased was a bachelor, in view of dependants are his minor brothers and also the mother, the Tribunal ought to have deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses, but the Tribunal has deducted at 50% and thereby assessed the loss of dependency at Rs.3,60,000/- and awarded Rs.2,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.2,500/-
towards funeral expenses, totally Rs.3,64,500/-.
Though the petitioners are entitled for higher compensation, since they have not filed any appeal, it is not proper to go into it.

10. With regard to liability is concerned, it is undisputed that the second respondent is the owner of the bus, third respondent is the insurer and the bus had been hired to fourth respondent/Corporation.

The contention of the Insurance Company that even though the bus was hired to the Corporation, it was not brought to its notice and endorsement in the policy is not incorporated and therefore, the Tribunal is right in directing the Corporation to pay the compensation.

In answer to it, learned counsel for the Corporation has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Managing Director, KSRTC - vs- New India Assurance Co.Ltd. and Another1 wherein similar circumstances has been dealt with, at para-28 of the judgment, which reads as follows:
"28.

entities.text: Managing Director, KSRTC - vs- New India Assurance Co.Ltd. and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The KSRTC can also be treated as owner for the purposes of Section 2(30) of the Act plying the buses under lease agreement.

The Insurance Company admittedly has insured the vehicle and taken the requisite premium and it is not a case set up by the insurer that intimation was not given to the insurance company of the hiring arrangement .
Even if the intimation had not been given, in our opinion, the insurer cannot escape the liability to indemnify as in the case of hiring of vehicle intimation is not required to be given.

It is only in the case of complete transfer of the vehicle when change of registration particulars are required under Section 157 of the Act, an intimation has to be given by the transferee for effecting necessary changes in the policy.
Even otherwise, that would be a ministerial act and the insurer cannot escape the liability for that reason.

When the KSRTC has become the owner of the vehicle during the period it was on hire with it for the purpose of Section 2(30) of the Act by virtue (2016) 2 SCC 382 of provisions contained in Section 157 of the Act, the insurance policy shall be deemed to be transferred.

As such, insurer is liable to make indemnification and cannot escape the liability so incurred by the KSRTC."
11.

Referring to the judgment in Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation -vs- Kulsum and Others2, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that when the vehicle given on hire by the owner of the vehicle to the State Road Transport Corporation with its existing the running insurance policy, it was held that the State Road Corporation have become the owner of the vehicle during the specified period The Divisional Controller vs Madhu on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165861954/
4 and vehicle having been insured at the instance of the original owner, it would be deemed that vehicle was transferred along with insurance policy to the State Road Transport Corporation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurer cannot escape the liability to pay compensation.
12. In that view, the contention raised by the Insurance Company has been answered.
When the (2011) 8 SCC 142 vehicle was hired by the State Road Transport Corporation, the ownership is transferred along with existing insurance policy.
As on the date of accident, the policy of insurance is intact and there is no allegation of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

Under such circumstances, the Insurance Company cannot avoid its liability to indemnify the owner i.e., the second respondent, who hired the vehicle to the Corporation and the Corporation being the deemed owner during the said period, the Insurance Company has to indemnify both the original owner and the deemed owner of the bus.
13. I have perused the impugned judgment.
The Tribunal though discussed that the vehicle in question was under the control of Corporation, it becomes the owner of the vehicle.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court as above, the Tribunal ought to have directed the Insurance Company to indemnify the owner, but it has gone on a wrong assumption that R.T.O. has not issued separate permit for the bus to ply in the route in which the accident had taken place.
The Tribunal is ignorant of amendment to Section 103(1-A) of the Amendment Act, its direction to the Corporation to pay compensation is erroneous.
It is not the petitioners' appeal, there is no question of excluding the interest for the period of 45 days, which the Insurance Company has sought for to exclude the interest for the said period.
Hence, the Insurance Company is required to indemnify the original owner and also the Corporation.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment is modified.

(iii) The respondent No.6 herein/Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the owner of the bus/5th respondent and also the deemed owner of the bus/appellant and directed to deposit the compensation along with interest as ordered by the Tribunal within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(v) The statutory amount deposited by NWKRTC shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records and it shall be refunded to it.
Sd/-
JUDGE KNM/-
